clue.text: Country cops it in knock out

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it is placed inside the second word's letters

blocks.note: to brain someone is to hit them hard on the head, knocking them out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation is punished for a knockout, as if a boxing bout went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops it' is British slang for getting punished, but here 'cops' only joins the definition to the wordplay; to brain someone is to knock them out with a blow to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is a sovereign nation, so it is an example of the general word for a state.

clue.text: Bring up some stars at fabulous awards ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: The BAFTAs are the British film and television awards.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Academy's annual prize event honours film and television achievements, so it is a showbusiness ceremony.

clue.text: Essentially sick earl must eventually hit the ground

the two central letters
the two central letters

explanation.surface: An ailing nobleman is bound to collapse in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings, which melted, and he fell to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical boy who flew with feathered wings plunged down after flying too high, a fall from the sky.

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the small problem pieces ahead of the shuffled word, though the clue lists them second.

clue.text: Starters in New Age diner include "ram's bottom"

clue.text: The French train provides space to stretch out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests a railway carriage, but it is a verb meaning to prepare someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the room available in front of a seat for a passenger's legs to extend.

clue.text: Such laws restrict service opportunities for landlords

definitions.text: Such laws restrict service opportunities for landlords

explanation.walkthrough: A British pub's keeper is called its landlord, and the law fixes when alcohol may be sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensing laws in Britain control when and where alcoholic drinks may be sold to customers.

clue.text: Come together with duke to cut off any further issue

D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Agreeing with a nobleman to settle a matter once and for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' here means offspring, so stopping any more of them means castration.
explanation.definitionFit: To geld an animal is to castrate it, ending its ability to produce offspring.

clue.text: Pour out more vino — I will  eat everything!

definitions.note: a self-description standing for the noun

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hungry, thirsty diner demands extra wine and declares they will eat anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore consumes both plants and meat, so it will happily eat any kind of food.

clue.text: Pads for comfortable shoes?

second meaning: shoes with no heel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pads' looks like cushioning for the feet, but it is slang for places to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a British apartment, and flats are also heel-less shoes worn for ease.

clue.text: Cut lights in place for ship-to-shore transmission

to light on something is to alight or come down on it

explanation.surface: Someone switching off the lamps at a coastal radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut lights' reads as killing the power; both words are verbs. The definition is playful: cargo passes from ship to shore at docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Docklands are harbour districts where vessels unload goods onto land, a humorous take on transferring things from sea to shore.

clue.text: Gemstone a queen pinned to a soldier

a standard abbreviation for queen
taken as written
a marine is a soldier serving with the navy

explanation.definitionFit: Aquamarine is a blue-green variety of beryl prized as a precious stone in jewellery.

clue.text: Finished shelter to exclude cold

C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A finished building keeps out the chill.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it has ended, so the word is a synonym for completed.

clue.text: Elizabeth understood serial killer being only out for himself

blocks.note: the queen's name abbreviated to its initial
if you got it, you understood it

explanation.surface: A queen grasped that a murderer was acting purely in his own interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego-tripper acts selfishly to boost their own self-image, caring for nobody else.

clue.text: Reagan let IRS shake up old currency group

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The sterling area was a historical bloc of countries that pegged their money to the British pound.

clue.text: They will sell you tales about stalkers

clue.text: Skimpy and close fitting women's clothing
